item.title: Stargazing - Perseids Meteor Shower — Wed Aug 12, 9:00 PM — TBD
item.description:
The Stargazing Devils are hosting a special stargazing session on Wednesday, August 12th from 9 PM to 11 PM -- back up dates on August 13th or 14th --for the Perseid meteor shower, which peaks August 12th and 13th.
Under clear, dark skies, watchers can expect to see roughly 50 to 100 swift, bright meteors and colorful fireballs per hour. The display is created as Earth passes through debris from the comet Swift-Tuttle. Source - NASA
Check the Duke Teaching Observatory website for more information and updates (see below).
Location TBD
Source: Duke University

item.description:
Carolina Tarwheels Cycling Club A regular Saturday group ride leaving from Wilson Park each Saturday. (occasionally Briar Chapel or Gold Park)
Route: To be posted by 8:00 PM on Thursday
What to expect:
* Ride length of \~60 miles, occasionally shorter/longer, at 20-21 mph * Max group size of 22. If there are more than that we will divide into two groups before the start. (Group 1 will be at the upper range of the target pace with significant efforts at the designated segments, Group 2 will start a few minutes later and will not be quite as intense.) * Double paceline ride with friendly and relaxed attitude/conversation * 10-15 minute stop along the way for hydration, fuel, and socializing * A few friendly and competitive "go hard" segments with a regroup at designated spots. (However, not a no-drop ride) * Post ride continue the social/beverage option
RSVP is required for all riders who either start at WP or plan to join the ride on the road.

item.title: Downtown Durham African American Historian-Guided Tour — Sat Aug 15, 4:00 PM — CCB Plaza
item.description:
Durham: the mecca of black capitalism and the center of North Carolina’s African American business community. Join a local historian on this guided walking tour of Durham’s Black Wall Street, hearing the stories of how a humble sharecropper became the owner of the largest black-ned company in American history, and seeing some of the sites related to their stories. Learn how businessmen, labor organizers, educated academics, and craftsmen each contributed to the unique history of Durham’s African American community.

item.title: Is Your Syllabus Ready? (In Person) — Mon Aug 17, 10:00 AM — Perkins Library
item.description:
Your syllabus is more than a course policy document - it is students' first introduction to your course and a roadmap for their learning. In this interactive workshop, you'll explore practical strategies for creating a syllabus that communicates expectations clearly, supports student success, and sets an inclusive and welcoming tone from the first day of class.
We'll share evidence-informed approaches, syllabus resources, and examples that you can immediately apply as you prepare for the semester. Leave with ideas to strengthen your syllabus and plan a meaningful first day of class. Join us to start the semester strong!

item.title: Hanes Visiting Artist Lecture Series: Jes Fan — Thu Sep 3, 5:30 PM — Hamilton Hall
item.description:
Department of Art and Art History
Jes Fan’s interdisciplinary practice explores the intersection of biology and identity, incorporating living matter, as well as invisible substances like melanin and hormones, that shape how we experience the world into their sculptures. Through this process, Fan looks at how these highly politicized materials form our understanding of the social constructs of race and gender, and the absurd pursuit of delimiting these as quantifiable amounts of material. Originally trained in glassmaking, Fan combines hand-blown cellular glass forms with casts made from sections of human bodies, in aqua resin and bearing uncanny flesh-like tones. Removed from the context of the figure, these forms take on abstract qualities, repeated and distorted across architectural armatures, suggesting an experience of the body increasingly intertwined with and mediated by technology.
Jes Fan lives and works in Brooklyn and Hong Kong. Fan's recent solo exhibition Unbounde
